explanation: Hostile-environment and retaliation case; Ledbetter cited only for the 180-day Alabama charge-filing period, with Morgan governing timeliness. No pay-setting accrual rule applied, so limb 1 fails though the 2008 charge postdates the Act's date.

Court cites Brockamp for no equitable exception to s.6511 where IRS mistakenly allowed a time-barred credit. No financial disability asserted; s.6511(h) left that part of Brockamp intact (own knowledge), so the holding applied is unaffected.

Appeal decided 1 July 2003, after the PROTECT Act; court reviews upward departures for abuse of discretion with Koon's substantial deference and affirms on that standard. No mention of the Act's de novo review in the text given (parts omitted).

Ledbetter cited only for the standard of review on judgment as a matter of law. No timeliness or pay-decision accrual issue decided; verdict for plaintiff affirmed. Limb 1 fails. Claim was pending past 28 May 2007.

Sexual-harassment hostile-environment appeal; Ledbetter cited solely for the Rule 50 review standard. No pay claim or charge-timeliness ruling, so limb 1 fails. Opinion gives no dates for the conduct or charge.

2008 Chapter 13 case; court values non-residential real property at replacement value under Rash. BAPCPA's s.506(a)(2) reaches only personal property and largely codifies replacement value (own knowledge), so Rash as applied to real estate was not overridden.

Withdrawal from university occurred May 2007, before the ADAAA's 1 January 2009 date, so pre-amendment law governed. Court recites Sutton's mitigating-measures rule but decides on lack of evidence of substantial limitation, not on mitigation.
